relevance_note: The paper singles out one individual CVID patient who carried a TNFAIP3 variant: "one CVID patient was later found to carry a monogenic TNFAIP3 variant", so at least one identifiable person with a TNFAIP3 variant is described.
method_note: Read the paper, schema and rules only; no script was used, all rows were written by hand from my reading of the Markdown. Scope: the only in-scope person is the single CD14+ CVID patient of the discovery cohort who carried a TNFAIP3 variant; the other CVID patients (including the T-cell patients without monogenic variants) and the plasma cohort are out of scope and are counted only in publications.cohort_size_as_stated. No label is printed for this person and no role word is used, so the label follows rule 6 (unnamed person 1). No variant description is printed anywhere (no cDNA, protein or genomic string, no transcript), so the variants row keeps variant_original_string = 'not reported' as the rules require; the variant is therefore not described and no variant class, zygosity, inheritance, functional, pathogenicity or ACMG value was recorded. The sentence "This TNFAIP3 variant was first described in a CVID patient in 2020 (34)" refers to a previously published patient of reference [34]; that person gets no row because the paper gives no individual-level fact (no sex, age, variant description or feature) beyond the diagnosis, and the statement is about the variant rather than about any of this paper's own patients, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false. Ambiguities: (1) the paper has two non-overlapping cohorts (6 CVID patients in the WGBS discovery cohort, 60 CVID patients in the plasma cohort) and never states a combined total; I recorded 60, the size of the main patient cohort the authors state. (2) study_type: this is an exploratory molecular (epigenetic/plasma protein) study of patient cohorts rather than a clinical case series; I chose 'case series/cohort'. (3) The paper gives the discovery patients' complication subgroup ("complicated CVID") only as a group statement naming the group, and does not say which complications this person had, so no phenotypic feature could be marked observed or excluded; phenotypic_features is empty and all 20 checklist items are 'not reported' for the individual. (4) The individual's monocyte finding ("hypomethylation in pathways related to Fc gamma receptor-mediated phagocytosis") is a molecular result, not a clinical feature, so it was not entered in phenotypic_features. (5) No stacked cells (' / ') occur in this paper's tables, and Table 1/Table 2 contain only group-level summary rows, so no table-symbol or stacked-cell rules applied. No contradictions between statements about this person were found.
